summary.text: Physics is the scientific study of matter, how it moves and behaves through space and time, and related ideas such as energy and force.
It became a separate science when early modern Europeans used experimental and quantitative methods to discover what are now considered its laws.
Advances in physics often enable new technologies, from television and computers to domestic appliances, and explain mechanisms that other sciences study.

facts.label: Its practitioners
facts.value: A scientist who specializes in physics is called a physicist

facts.label: Aristotle's reach
facts.value: Aristotelian physics was influential for about two millennia

facts.label: Atomism's long wait
facts.value: Proposed by Leucippus and Democritus, found correct about 2000 years later

facts.label: Age of the field
facts.value: One of the oldest academic disciplines

items.prompt: A philosopher decides that heavier things must fall faster, using a clever argument, and never drops anything to check. Which feature of Aristotle's approach does this match?

options.label: Repeated experiments measured the fall and confirmed it
Logical argument without experimental verification of the result
Calculus applied to the motion of falling objects
Rejecting natural causes in favor of divine ones

items.explain: His approach mixed limited observation with logical deduction and did not rely on experimental verification, and he held that heavier objects fall faster.

items.prompt: Aristotle watches a campfire on the ground and sees the flames leap upward. How would his theory of elements explain this?

options.label: A second object keeps applying force to push the flames up
The flames are drawn toward the stars, which are gods
Fire belongs at the top, so flames head back toward their natural place
Denser air beneath the flames lifts them in proportion to weight

items.explain: Each of the four elements had a natural place, with fire at the top, and an element away from its place moves toward it.

items.prompt: Chemistry, biology and physics were once all part of one broad field of study. What changed so that physics became its own science?

options.label: People tested ideas with experiments and measurement to find laws
Philosophers stopped asking questions about motion and matter
Scholars returned to the theory of four natural elements
Invaders ended study of the natural world in Europe

items.explain: Physics became a separate science when early modern Europeans used experimental and quantitative methods to discover its laws.

items.prompt: A friend says physics is just abstract theory with no effect on daily life. Which reply fits what physics has actually done?

options.label: It only serves other sciences and never builds technology
Its influence ended once natural philosophy broke apart
Its main product has been a Latin word, physica
Electromagnetism and solid-state physics led to computers

items.explain: Advances in electromagnetism, solid-state physics and nuclear physics led directly to technologies that transformed modern society.

items.prompt: In ancient Greece, Thales said every event has a natural cause, not a supernatural one. What were thinkers like him doing?

options.label: Worshipping the stars and planets as gods
Rejecting non-naturalistic explanations for natural phenomena
Building a framework around a prime mover
Developing calculus to solve physical problems

items.explain: Pre-Socratic philosophers like Thales rejected non-naturalistic explanations and proclaimed that every event had a natural cause.

items.prompt: Ancient Greeks thought we see because rays go out from the eye. What alternative did Ibn al-Haytham present in his Book of Optics?

options.label: A full theory of how images form
Four elements that each seek a natural place
The idea of light rays
The claim that all matter is made of atoms

items.explain: He presented light rays as an alternative to the Greek idea of visual rays, though he still lacked the concept of image formation.
